chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Shall I inform you of those upon whom the Fire will be forbidden tomorrow?" They said, "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said, "The humble, the gentle, the close [of kin], and the easy-going."

key_terms.الْقَرِيبُ: The close (one who maintains kinship ties)
key_terms.الْهَيْنُ: The humble or lowly in status

ai.seo_question: What are the four character traits that save a person from the Fire according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the ethical foundation of salvation, emphasizing that social ease (husn al-khuluq) and humility are not merely polite manners but decisive factors in divine mercy. In Shia tradition, these traits reflect the imams' character and serve as practical criteria for believers to evaluate their spiritual standing, linking inner piety with outward social conduct.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-83 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Sa’dan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Sa’dan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“Do you want me to tell you from whom the fire will be forbidden in the Hereafter? The people said, “O Prophet of God! Yes.” God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Humble ones; sociable ones; helpful ones; and simple ones.”
